minutes.headline: Committee approved the high school late fee plan and recommended middle school sports at a $200 fee after seeing the cost breakdown.
minutes.summary: The committee held its reorganization, took line-item transfers, approved minutes and a corrected school calendar, and heard a long public comment on middle school athletics fees. It approved the high school athletics proposal with a sliding scale for the reduced-lunch fee, then approved middle school athletics after the athletic director read a cost breakdown. The facilities-use rate proposal was held to the next meeting and the blizzard bag pilot was postponed.

public_comment.topic: A parent asked the committee to consider waiving facility fees for the primary school Girl Scouts.
A resident questioned the late registration fee and the middle school fee, citing the burden on reduced-lunch families.
A parent said the jump in the middle school fee is large and asked for substantiation, comparing neighbouring districts and raising field space.
A parent and middle school track coach said the fee jump is large, coach pay is low and the team lacks track access; supported the late fee.
A parent supported the middle school sports proposal.
A parent supported the proposal but objected to short notice on important topics.
A resident urged revisiting the public comment policy and said the reduced-lunch figures cited earlier were incorrect.
A resident asked whether the fee would be moved into the budget later and asked to see the numbers behind the fee.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to recommend the middle school athletics proposal after the athletic director read a per-sport cost breakdown.
The committee approved the high school athletics proposal, with the reduced-lunch fee changed to a sliding scale.
The facilities use rate proposal was held to the June 5 meeting for approval.
The committee voted to accept the superintendent's recommendation to postpone the blizzard bag pilot.
The committee approved the 2019-2020 school calendar with changes, accepted line-item transfers, and voted on reorganization.

why_it_matters: Athletics user fees and the late registration fee fall on families, and the reduced-lunch fee and sliding scale decide what lower-income households pay for a child to play.
The facilities use rates would replace youth sports contracts, so some local groups that rent school space may see higher charges.
